problems.title: Largest and smallest decimals from three digits
problems.question: Use digits 1,2,4 once each to form decimals with digits on both sides of the decimal point. How much larger is the greatest than the least?
problems.idea: Place the largest digits before the decimal for the maximum, and the smallest first for the minimum.

problems.title: Count positive divisors by prime factorization
problems.question: How many positive divisors does 6³·3⁶ have?
problems.idea: Collect prime powers.
steps: A divisor independently chooses the exponent of 2 from 0,…,3 and of 3 from 0,…,9.
Multiply the choice counts.

problems.title: Fruit-bearing trees after a cancellation
problems.question: An orchard contains only apple and pear trees. The number of fruit-bearing pears equals the number of non-fruit-bearing apples. There are 25 apple trees. How many trees bear fruit?
problems.idea: Replace the fruit-bearing pear count by the missing apple count.
formulas: Let non-fruiting apples=n; fruiting apples=25−n; fruiting pears=n.
steps: The total bearing fruit is (25−n)+n.

problems.title: Reverse a percentage comparison
problems.question: The first number is 0.4 times the second. What percent of the first is the second?
problems.idea: Invert the ratio before converting to a percentage.
steps: Multiply by 100%.

problems.title: Guarantee three usable shoe pairs
problems.question: A box has five red and six black pairs of equal-size shoes. How many shoes must be drawn blindly to guarantee three matching left-right pairs?
problems.idea: Count the most shoes that can be drawn while making at most two pairs.
steps: The two maximum counts are at most 5 and 6. If there are at most two usable pairs, the sum of the two minimum counts is at most 2.
Thus at most 5+6+2=13 shoes can avoid three pairs. This is achievable with all 11 left shoes and two right shoes.
One more shoe forces at least three pairs.

problems.title: Annulus area from a tangent chord
problems.question: Two circles are concentric. A chord of the larger circle of length 16 is tangent to the smaller. Find the annulus area.
problems.idea: The radius to the chord’s midpoint is the smaller radius.
steps: The squared-radius difference is 64.

problems.title: Angles compared by percentages
problems.question: In a triangle, A is 20% greater than B and B is 25% greater than C. Find B.
problems.idea: Use a common unit for all three angles.
steps: The 15 ratio units total 180°, so each is 12°.

problems.title: A sum of periodic functions need not have a least period
problems.question: f and g have least positive periods T₁,T₂. Which listed expression must be the least positive period of f+g?
problems.idea: Cancellation and incompatible periods prevent a universal formula.
formulas: Example f=sin x,g=−sin x gives f+g=0.
steps: The zero function has every positive period, so it has no least positive period.
Also sums with incommensurable periods can fail to be periodic. Thus neither a common-multiple formula, sum, nor minimum is guaranteed.
problems.answer: None of the listed formulas is necessarily valid.

problems.title: Reflect a parabola across the x-axis
problems.question: Reflect y=3(x−1)²+2 across the x-axis.
problems.idea: A reflection across the x-axis negates every output.
steps: Distribute the minus sign.
problems.note: The scan does not clearly name the reflection axis. This answer assumes the x-axis. If the y-axis is intended instead, the reflected equation is y=3(x+1)²+2.

problems.title: Circumradius from two sides and an included angle
problems.question: AB=6,AC=9,angle A=120°. Find the circumradius.
problems.idea: Find the opposite side with the cosine rule.
steps: BC=3√19. Divide by √3 to get the circumradius.

problems.title: Equivalent quadratic equations have proportional coefficients
problems.question: x²+mx+n=0 is equivalent to 3x²+2x−5=0. Find m+n.
problems.idea: Normalize the second equation to leading coefficient 1.
steps: The two distinct roots determine the same monic quadratic, so m=2/3,n=−5/3.
Add them.

problems.title: Three absolute-value statements
problems.question: Which of |x|=|−x|, |x+y|≤|x|+|y|, and |x−y|≥||x|−|y|| hold for all real inputs?
problems.idea: Use sign symmetry, the triangle inequality and the reverse triangle inequality.
steps: The first statement is absolute-value symmetry. The second is the triangle inequality.
For the third, |x|≤|x−y|+|y| and the swapped version give both bounds needed for the absolute difference.
problems.note: The scan’s third statement omits the outer absolute value on the right; that weaker version is also always true.

problems.title: Angle between two diagonals of a regular pentagon
problems.question: Find the angle between the two diagonals from one vertex of a regular pentagon.
problems.idea: It is an inscribed angle subtending one side arc.
formulas: Each side arc is 360°/5=72°; an inscribed angle is half its intercepted arc.
steps: Half of 72° is 36°.

problems.title: Two semicircular segments
problems.question: Two equal semicircles have radius 2 cm. B,D are the arc midpoints in the printed S-shaped diagram. Find the total shaded area.
problems.idea: The shading consists of two equal 90° circular segments.
steps: Each sector has area π. Its triangle has perpendicular radius sides 2,2, so area 2.
Each shaded segment is π−2; there are two.

problems.title: Maximize a sign expression
problems.question: For abc≠0, S=1+|a|/a+2|b|/b+3|ab|/(ab)−4|c|/c. Find Smax−Smin.
problems.idea: The sign of ab is the product of the signs of a,b, not an independent choice.
formulas: Set s=sign a,t=sign b,u=sign c; S=1+s+2t+3st−4u.
steps: Choosing u independently gives maximum 1+6+4=11 and minimum 1−4−4=−7.
Their difference is 18.
problems.note: None of the printed values 12,14,22,20 equals the correct difference 18.

problems.title: Bisectors of adjacent supplementary angles
problems.question: What is the angle between bisectors of adjacent angles forming a straight line?
problems.idea: Their half-angles add to half a straight angle.
steps: The bisectors are perpendicular.

problems.title: A sine from a dot product
problems.question: Vectors have lengths 8 and 15 and dot product 72. Find the sine of their angle.
problems.idea: First find its cosine.
steps: The vector angle lies in [0,π], so its sine is nonnegative.

problems.title: A square root is an absolute value
problems.question: Solve √(4x²−4x+1)≤1−2x.
problems.idea: Recognize the square.
steps: The inequality |u|≤−u holds exactly when u≤0.
Thus 2x−1≤0.

problems.title: Area on a scaled map
problems.question: A city covers 144 km². Find its area in cm² on a 1:600000 map.
problems.idea: Convert one map centimetre to the real distance.
formulas: 1 cm represents 600000 cm=6 km; 1 cm² represents 36 km².
steps: Map area=144/36.

problems.title: Travel farther after a speed increase
problems.question: A car covers 60 km in 40 minutes, then increases speed by 30 km/h. How far does it go at the new speed in the same time?
problems.idea: Convert 40 minutes to 2/3 hour.
formulas: Original speed=60/(2/3)=90 km/h; new speed=120 km/h.
steps: Distance=120·2/3.

problems.title: Use a newly defined operation
problems.question: If a*b=5a−2b, solve (x+2)*(x−1)=18.
problems.idea: Substitute directly into the operation rule.

problems.title: Which perimeter information is sufficient?
problems.question: Altitudes BE,DF of parallelogram ABCD form square BFDE. I: triangle ABE has perimeter 20. II: square BFDE has perimeter 32. Which conditions determine the parallelogram perimeter?
problems.idea: The triangle perimeter is exactly half the parallelogram perimeter.
formulas: Let AE=t, BE=ED=h. Then AD=t+h and AB=√(t²+h²).
steps: Triangle ABE perimeter=t+h+AB=AD+AB.
Therefore I alone gives parallelogram perimeter 2·20=40.
II fixes h=8 but leaves t free, so it does not determine AD+AB.
problems.answer: I alone is sufficient; II alone is not. The perimeter from I is 40 cm.

problems.title: Area scales as the square of circumference
problems.question: A circle’s circumference increases by 30%. By what percent does its area increase?
problems.idea: Radius scales in the same ratio as circumference.
steps: Subtract 1 and multiply by 100%.

problems.title: A condition on every group of six
problems.question: Among 25 students, every six include at least three girls. What is the greatest possible number of boys?
problems.idea: Four boys would let us choose a violating six-person group.
formulas: If boys≥4, choose four boys and two others to get at most two girls.
steps: Thus there can be at most 3 boys.
With exactly 3 boys and 22 girls, every six contain at least 3 girls, so the bound is attainable.

problems.title: A machine’s fraction of a larger job
problems.question: An excavator digs a channel in m hours. What fraction of a channel twice as long does it dig in a hours at the same rate?
problems.idea: Measure output relative to the doubled job.
formulas: The doubled job takes 2m hours; fraction completed in a hours=a/(2m).
steps: This is the requested fraction, provided a is within the time needed for the job.

problems.title: Scale a transport workload
problems.question: Three trucks move 360 tonnes over 30 km in 4 hours. How many identical trucks move 630 tonnes over 50 km in 5 hours?
problems.idea: Assume truck work is proportional to tonne-kilometres and available time.
steps: The factors simplify to 3·7/4·5/3·4/5=7.
problems.answer: 7 trucks, under the stated proportional-work model.

problems.title: Compose two linear functions
problems.question: f(x)=2−3x,g(x)=2−5x. Find f(g(x)).
problems.idea: Use g(x) as the input to f.
steps: Expand: 2−6+15x.

problems.title: A sector label that names an external point
problems.question: A circle touches the sides of angle ABC=60° at A,C. AC=6. The question asks for sector AOB.
problems.idea: Distinguish the sector between the two contact radii from the sector in the direction of the external vertex.
steps: The sector AOC has area (120/360)π·12=4π, matching a printed choice.
B is an external point, so AOB is not a standard sector named by two circle points. The ray OB bisects angle AOC, giving angle AOB=60°.
If “AOB” means the sector between rays OA,OB, its area is 2π.
problems.answer: Intended contact-point sector AOC: 4π. Literal ray sector AOB: 2π.
problems.note: The source prints AOB but B is the external angle vertex. The listed 4π corresponds to correcting that label to AOC.

problems.title: Perimeter of a tangential trapezoid
problems.question: A trapezoid circumscribed about a circle has midline 199 cm. Find its perimeter.
problems.idea: Tangency makes the leg sum equal the base sum.
steps: The perimeter is 796 cm.
problems.note: The printed choice 769 appears to transpose the last two digits. The correct value is 796.

problems.title: Four tangent circles inside a 60° angle
problems.question: Four circles are each tangent to both sides of a 60° angle, successively tangent to one another and increasing away from the vertex. Find their total area divided by the smallest area.
problems.idea: The centres lie on the angle bisector.
formulas: Centre distance from vertex=r/sin30°=2r. For adjacent radii R>r, 2(R−r)=R+r.
steps: Thus R=3r, so consecutive areas have ratio 9.
The four relative areas are 1,9,81,729.
Their sum is 820.

problems.title: An absolute value around a positive quadratic
problems.question: For f(x)=x²−x+1, find the minimum of |f(x)|+2.
problems.idea: Complete the square to show f is always positive.
steps: Therefore |f|=f. Its minimum is 3/4 at x=1/2.
Add 2.

problems.title: Area of a parallelogram from vectors
problems.question: Find the area of the parallelogram on vectors (4,3) and (6,8).
problems.idea: Use the absolute determinant.

problems.title: When a linear parameter equation is solvable
problems.question: Find the conditions on a,b for ax−b=bx+2 to have at least one solution.
problems.idea: Collect the x terms and separate the zero coefficient case.
steps: If a≠b, there is one solution x=(b+2)/(a−b).
If a=b, the equation is solvable only when b+2=0. That gives a=b=−2 and every x works.

problems.title: A sum of nonnegative terms must vanish
problems.question: Solve x²−4xy+√[(x²−1)²]+4y²=0.
problems.idea: Group the quadratic and identify the absolute value.
steps: Both summands are nonnegative, so both must be zero.
x²=1 gives x=±1; x=2y gives y=x/2.

problems.title: Range of a bounded rational function
problems.question: Find the range of y=3x/(x²+9).
problems.idea: Use (x−3)²≥0 and (x+3)²≥0.
steps: Dividing by 2(x²+9)>0 gives −1/2≤y≤1/2.
The endpoints occur at x=−3 and x=3. Continuity gives every value between them.

problems.title: The triangle whose sides are medians
problems.question: A triangle’s three medians equal the side lengths of a second triangle. Find the ratio of the first triangle’s area to the second.
problems.idea: The three directed median vectors sum to zero and form a triangle.
steps: Their sum is zero. The absolute determinant of the first two is 3/4 times |det(u,v)|.
Triangle area is half the determinant magnitude, so the median-sided triangle has 3/4 of the original area.
Thus the original-to-new area ratio is 4:3.

problems.title: Walking on a moving escalator
problems.question: Two people descend a moving escalator. One walks twice as fast as the other and counts 60 steps while the other counts 40. How many steps are visible when the escalator is stopped?
problems.idea: Their counted steps equal walking speed relative to the escalator times elapsed time.
formulas: Let walking speeds 2u,u and escalator speed v, all in steps per second.
steps: The fast walker’s time is 60/(2u)=30/u; the slow walker’s is 40/u.
If N is the fixed escalator length, N=(2u+v)30/u=60+30v/u and N=(u+v)40/u=40+40v/u.
Equating gives v/u=2, then N=120.

problems.title: Minimize the distance between quadratic roots
problems.question: For which m is the distance between roots of x²+(m−2)x=2m+15 smallest?
problems.idea: For a monic real quadratic the root separation is √D.
steps: This is positive for every m and minimized when m=−2.
The minimum root distance is √60=2√15.
